newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market down to 10.4 vs 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market down to 10.4 vs 11.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate dropped to 10.4 from 11.2 percent on Tuesday, as call money loans representing most of the trade weighed down the rates, dealers said.
They put daily settlements at 42.5 million kuna against a 54.5 million kuna demand.
Fresh trade accounted for 30.3 million kuna and included mostly call money loans granted at a steady 10.5 percent rate.
The central bank bought 11.1 million marks to help the liquidity-plagued money market by injecting just under 40 million kuna into the banking sector in two days.
Insurers rolled over previous funds at nine percent for one-week loans and 11 percent for two-week borrowings.
Banks charged 11 percent for renewed one-week funds.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrate for Wednesday firmer at 6.0469 against the dollar and weaker at 3.5700 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
